      - heading "What's happening?" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Each point shows a data value. The dashed line is the mean. Segments show deviations, and squares represent squared deviations.
      - heading "Why square deviations?" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Squaring makes every deviation positive and penalises points farther from the mean.
      - heading "Common misconception" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Use n − 1 for sample variance and N for the entire population. Using n for a sample underestimates spread.
      - heading "In Words" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Variance is the average of squared deviations from the mean. Standard deviation is the square root of variance.
      - heading "Formula (Sample)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: s² = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² / (n − 1)
      - paragraph: s = √s²
      - heading "Formula (Population)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: σ² = Σ(xᵢ − μ)² / N
      - paragraph: σ = √σ²
